_comment: FINAL-RELEASE-PRODUCTION-READY-01 / 01A — canonical provisioning order for a Directus environment.
This file is the single source of ORDER. docs/project/RELEASE-SAFETY-GATES.md §3A.8 is the
normative contract that requires these steps; this manifest is its executable expression, and
scripts/provision-directus.mjs is the only thing that executes it. A runbook must reference this
file rather than restate the order, so the order can never drift between three places.
Why the steps exist at all: a Directus YAML schema snapshot captures collections, fields and
relations only. Triggers, functions, database constraints, and every role / policy / access link
and permission row are NOT in it, so a fresh environment built from the snapshot alone is
silently incomplete. Each SQL artifact below is the canonical rebuild source for one of those
missing pieces.
Ownership is deliberately not shared. Each artifact declares what it owns and writes nothing
else, so two steps can never fight over the same row:
· 10  schema baseline      — collections, fields, relations
· 31  access bootstrap     — role nuxt-server, policy site-readonly-policy, their access link,
and the service user structure (no credential)
· 32  service token        — one column of one row: directus_users.token. SECRET, NOT GIT DATA
· 40  permissions-01       — the three D-034 Content read rows
· 50  permissions-02       — the sixteen FINAL-RELEASE-FIX-E legacy site rows
· 60  media folders        — the ten Protected System Folder rows of directus_folders (D-045):
home, applications, company, products, resources and the five
product categories. Never a legacy, frozen or customer folder
Steps 00–51 are what RELEASE-SAFETY-GATES §3A.8 requires. Step 60 comes from D-045: a fresh
environment gets the folder skeleton the Media Library's folder governance is keyed on. It
depends only on step 00, which creates directus_folders, and runs last so that the verified
chain before it keeps its order; step 61 verifies it immediately.
Step 32 is the one step whose input is a secret. It reads DIRECTUS_TOKEN, the same variable the
running Nuxt server reads from its own process environment, and installs its value: one secret
under one name, supplied once (FINAL-RELEASE-PRODUCTION-READY-01B / 01C). No value is stored here, in the SQL
artifact, or anywhere else in this repository; a deployment environment or secret manager owns
it. Missing secret fails the run closed — the environment is reported as not provisioned rather
than provisioned without a working runtime credential.
Business data is deliberately absent: provisioning builds an empty, correctly-shaped environment.
The ten system folders are structure the runtime expects, not content: no file, product, content
item or customer folder is created. Seeding real content is a separate, human activity.

steps.description: Create the Directus system tables and the first administrator on an empty database.

Apply the tracked collection / field / relation baseline. cc-imp-01-after.yaml is the canonical baseline because it is byte-identical to a snapshot of the verified environment; cc-imp-01-apply.yaml is the CC-IMP-01 transition input, not a current-state baseline.
Composite, partial and CHECK constraints a Directus snapshot cannot express.
Atomic draft-revision trigger and function. Must follow the constraints.
Archive / restore concurrency triggers. Order fixed by §3A.8: constraints then revision guard then lifecycle guard.

steps.inline: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_trigger t JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = t.tgrelid WHERE NOT t.tgisinternal AND c.relname IN ('content_items','content_item_locales','content_items_files','content_relations')) = 7 THEN 'schema_objects_verify: OK' ELSE 'schema_objects_verify: FAIL' END;
steps.description: Seven user triggers must exist: one revision guard plus six lifecycle guards.

DIRECTUS-ACCESS-BOOTSTRAP-01 — role nuxt-server, policy site-readonly-policy, the access link between them, and the credential-free service user. Must precede both permission artifacts: they own rows on a policy that has to exist already, and fail closed when it does not. Owns no permission row and no secret.

SECRET STEP, NOT GIT DATA. Installs DIRECTUS_TOKEN — the one secret, which the running Nuxt server also reads from its process environment — as the static token of the service user created by step 31. The value comes from the environment and is never written to, read from or logged by this repository. Absent secret fails the run closed; --without-service-token provisions the structure only and says so, leaving the environment unable to serve.

Mandatory verification of the identity structure before any permission row is written: one role, one least-privilege policy, one role-scoped access link, one active password-free service user, and that policy reachable from nothing else. Structure only — it never reads the token.
D-034 — the three nuxt-server Content read rows. Owns only those rows.
Mandatory verification immediately after the stage that wrote those rows.
FINAL-RELEASE-FIX-E — the sixteen legacy site rows, least privilege. Must run after artifact 01 and never touches its rows.
Mandatory verification. Also re-checks that the three D-034 rows are untouched.

MEDIA-LIBRARY-PRODUCTION-BOOTSTRAP-01 (D-045) — creates the missing Protected System Folders (home, applications, company, products, resources, and products/xray, products/metal-detection, products/checkweigher, products/combination, products/conveyor) and keeps every existing one with its UUID. Writes directus_folders rows and nothing else; never updates, moves or deletes a folder. Refuses, writing nothing, on a duplicate or case-variant canonical folder, a canonical name outside the customer zones away from its canonical position, a parent cycle, a folder name containing "/" or an unexpected table shape. Depends only on step 00.

Mandatory verification immediately after step 60: each of the ten canonical paths is held by exactly one folder, and none of the refusal conditions holds. Legacy and frozen folders of an older environment are not its concern.

postSteps: Restart Directus: it caches schema, policies and permissions in process memory, so a freshly provisioned environment serves the old shape until it restarts.
Run npm run release:check-test-data against the target database; only exit 0 passes.

The running Nuxt server authenticates with this same DIRECTUS_TOKEN, read from its process environment at run time: one secret, one name, supplied once from the deployment's secret manager. A build needs no secret (runbook §2).
Production additionally requires a verified restorable backup before any mutation, and a written rollback plan (§3A.8 steps 7 and 8). Neither is implemented by this script.
